paper.title: Multi-Player Bandits -- a Musical Chairs Approach

settings.name_in_paper: Static multi-player MAB with collisions (no communication)
unmapped: N players choose arms simultaneously; colliding players get zero reward and observe a collision indicator
no communication; number of players N unknown to players; N < K
regret against the best static allocation of players to the top-N arms
settings.definition_quote: R := \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{k\in K^{\ast}_t} \mu_k(t) - \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{j=1}^N \mu_j(t) (1 - \eta_j(t)) ... We define a collision as the event where more than one player chose the same arm at a given round, and assume that no reward is obtained in that case.

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic multi-player MAB (players enter and leave)
unmapped: players dynamically enter and leave; total number of entries/exits bounded by x (known to tune epoch length)
players may only enter/leave after the learning period of each epoch
shared clock between players, no communication
collisions give zero reward; regret against best allocation of current N_t players to top N_t arms
settings.definition_quote: one where the set of players, and therefore number of players N, is fixed and another where the number of players, N_t, can change at any round t ... we assume that the overall number of players entering and leaving is sublinear in T.

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic multi-player MAB scenario: second player enters at T/2, first leaves at T/2+fT (lower bound for MEGA)
unmapped: players enter and leave at specified rounds; collisions give zero reward
settings.definition_quote: the simple setting of two players and two arms, where the second player enters at some round in the game and the first player then leaves at some later round.

symbols.T_0: length of the exploration phase: ceil(max(K/2 ln(2K^2/delta), 16K/eps^2 ln(4K^2/delta), K^2 log(2/delta_2)/0.02))

conditions: gap Delta between N-th and (N+1)-th best arm is positive
tuning: T_0 set as in the theorem

source.label: thm:MC
source.quote: Let $\Delta>0$ be the gap between the expected reward of the $N$th best arm and the $N+1$ best arm. Then for all $\epsilon<\Delta$ and $\delta\in (0,1)$, with probability $ \geq 1 - \delta $, the expected regret of $ N $ players using the MC algorithm with $ K $ arms for $ T $ rounds, with parameter $T_0$ set to ... is at most \[ T_0 \cdot N + 2 \cdot \exp(2) \cdot N^2 . \]

results.notes: Bound is expected regret conditioned on an event of probability >= 1-delta (correct ranking and N estimated). Independent of T. T_0 scales as K log(K/delta)/eps^2 + K^2 log(1/delta).

symbols.x: upper bound on the total number of players entering and leaving during T rounds

conditions: N_m <= K upper bound on active players
minimal gap among best N_m+1 arms has known lower bound epsilon > 0
players enter/leave only after learning period of each epoch
tuning: Theta(sqrt(xT)) epochs with O~(1) learning rounds each

source.label: thm:DMC
source.quote: Let $N_m\leq K$ be an upper bound on the number of active players at any time point; ... and $x$ be an upper bound on the total number of players entering and leaving during $T$ rounds. Then with arbitrarily high probability, the expected regret of the DMC algorithm (over the rewards), using $\Theta(\sqrt{xT})$ epochs with $\tilde{O}(1)$ learning rounds at the beginning of each epoch, is at most: $\tilde{O} ( \sqrt{xT})$

results.notes: O~ hides log factors in T, delta and polynomial factors in Delta_min, K, N_m. Conditional expected regret on high-probability event.

bound.expression_latex: \frac{T}{T_1} \cdot \left( N_m \cdot \left(T_0 + 2 \cdot T_f \right)\right) + e\cdot 2 \left(T_1 - T_0 \right) + l\left(T_1 - T_0 \right)

symbols.T_0: learning-phase length with confidence delta/(2T), O(log T)
symbols.T_f: expected time for a player to fix on an arm, at most exp(2)*N_m
symbols.N_m: upper bound on number of active players

conditions: Delta_min lower bound on gaps among the best N_m+1 arms
players enter/leave only after learning period
tuning: T_0 = ceil(max(K/2 ln(2K^2/(delta/2T)), 16K/eps^2 ln(4K^2/(delta/2T)), K^2 log(4T/delta)/0.02))

source.label: lemma:DMC
source.quote: Then $\forall \delta\in (0,1)$ and $\epsilon < \Delta_{\min}$, w.p. $ \geq 1 - \delta $, the expected regret of the Dynamic MC algorithm played for $ T $ rounds, with parameters: ... and $ T_1$ chosen such that $ T_1 > T_0 $, is at most \[ \frac{T}{T_1} \cdot ( N_m \cdot (T_0 + 2 \cdot T_f )) + e\cdot 2 (T_1 - T_0 ) + l(T_1 - T_0 ). \]

results.notes: Proof's final sum uses e*N_m instead of 2e; recorded as stated in lemma.

symbols.f: fraction of T between second player entering and first leaving

conditions: applies to the MEGA algorithm for all choices of c,d,beta,p_0
second player enters at ceil(T/2), first leaves at ceil(T/2 + fT)

source.label: thm:discuss2
source.quote: Then for all choices of the MEGA algorithm parameters $c,d,\beta,p_0$, if $ \alpha $ ... is chosen such that $ \alpha \leq 1-\frac{4\log(4fT)}{T} $, and $f$ is chosen such that ... then: The expected regret of the MEGA algorithm is $ \Omega (T ) $.

results.notes: Lower bound for a specific algorithm (MEGA) on a specific scenario, not a minimax lower bound.

source.label: thm:discuss2
source.quote: The conditional expected regret of the DMC algorithm (using $\Theta(\sqrt{T})$ epochs) is $\tilde{O} (\sqrt{T} ) $.

results.notes: Conditional on high-probability event of correct ranking; special case of Theorem 2 with x=2.

symbols.lambda_rate: players alternately leave/enter every T^lambda rounds, lambda < 1

conditions: one player leaving every 2r*ceil(T^lambda) rounds and one entering every (2r+1)*ceil(T^lambda) rounds

source.label: thm:discuss1
source.quote: In the multi-player MAB setting with one player leaving every $(2 \cdot r) \cdot \lceil T^\lambda \rceil$ rounds, and one player entering every $(2 \cdot r + 1) \cdot \lceil T^\lambda\rceil $ rounds, ... The expected regret upper bound of the DMC algorithm is $\tilde{O} ( T^{1- \frac{\lambda}{2}} )$

results.notes: Corollary of Theorem 2 with x = T^{1-lambda}. Part 1 of the theorem concerns the MEGA upper-bound analysis, not a regret bound, so not recorded.
